title: ElementCollection in JPA (Spring Boot) | Alternative to @OneToMany
description:
#JavaTechie  #SpringBoot   #JPA   #Microservice

In this video, we will understand how to use ElementCollection in JPA with a complete Spring Boot example.

In most applications, we use @OneToMany to model relationships, but in many real-world scenarios, this can introduce unnecessary complexity like additional entities, relationship management, and extra boilerplate code.

Here, we will explore a simpler alternative using:
- @ElementCollection
- @Embeddable

We will implement a complete example step by step and compare it with @OneToMany to understand the differences clearly.

📌 In this video, you will learn:
- What is @ElementCollection in JPA
- How to use @Embeddable in Spring Boot
- Difference between @OneToMany and @ElementCollection
- When to use ElementCollection
- When NOT to use it (important for production)

💡 This approach is very useful when your child data does not need its own identity.

title: How Netflix Streams Videos | HLS Streaming with Spring Boot 🚀
description:
#JavaTechie  #SpringBoot   #HLS   #NetflixStream

🚀 Learn gRPC with Spring Boot in one complete Crash Course!

In this video, we will explore how Netflix streams videos efficiently using HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) and how you can build a similar video streaming system using Spring Boot.

Traditional video streaming downloads the entire video before playback, which causes buffering and slow start times. Modern platforms like Netflix, YouTube, and Amazon Prime solve this problem by splitting videos into small chunks and streaming them dynamically.

This technique is called HLS (HTTP Live Streaming).

In this tutorial, we will learn:

✅ How modern video streaming works
✅ What is HLS (HTTP Live Streaming)
✅ Why videos are split into small chunks (.ts segments)
✅ How .m3u8 playlists control streaming
✅ How Netflix-like streaming avoids buffering
✅ How to implement video streaming using Spring Boot + FFmpeg

By the end of this video, you will understand the complete architecture behind modern video streaming platforms and how to implement it in your Spring Boot applications.

title: 🚀 Production-Grade Null Safety in Spring Boot 4 | Stop NPEs Forever !
description:
#JavaTechie  #SpringBoot   #Realtime

🚀 NullPointerException crashes production apps — Spring Boot 4 can stop it at build time.

In real-world backend systems, a small API change can easily break multiple client applications. As your product evolves, new features demand API changes — but you cannot afford to break existing consumers.

That’s exactly where API Versioning becomes critical.

NullPointerException is one of the most common production issues in Spring applications.

In this video, you’ll learn how to implement production-grade null safety in Spring Boot 4 using JSpecify and NullAway.

We’ll see how compile-time null checks can prevent runtime NPEs and make your Spring applications safer and more reliable.

If you’re building real-world Spring Boot applications, this approach is a must.

title: 🚀 Spring Boot 4 API Versioning – Stop Breaking Client APIs
description:
#JavaTechie  #SpringBoot #Realtime

🚀 Stop Breaking Client APIs with Spring Boot 4 API Versioning

In real-world backend systems, a small API change can easily break multiple client applications. As your product evolves, new features demand API changes — but you cannot afford to break existing consumers.

That’s exactly where API Versioning becomes critical.

In this video, you’ll learn how to implement API Versioning in Spring Boot 4 using the new native versioning support — without creating messy V1, V2 controller classes.

We’ll cover:

✅ Why API versioning is important in production systems
✅ Problems with the old V1 / V2 controller approach
✅ Spring Boot 4 native API versioning architecture
✅ Path-based versioning
✅ Header-based versioning
✅ Query parameter versioning
✅ Media type versioning
✅ Real-world payment API example
✅ Best practices for scalable backend design

By the end of this video, you’ll be able to design backward-compatible APIs that evolve safely without breaking your clients.

title: Java Stream Gatherers Explained 🚀 | The Next Evolution of Streams  @Javatechie
description:
#JavaTechie   #Java   #stream    

Java 8’s Stream API was a game-changer — giving us functional-style operations like map, filter, flatMap, reduce, and collectors to make working with collections clean and expressive.
But as powerful as Streams are, they have limitations:

You can’t easily reuse stream logic (filter + map combos).

No built-in support for batching records.

Running IO-intensive tasks concurrently in streams is tricky.

That’s where Stream Gatherers (JEP 485, Java 21+) come in! 🎉

In this video, I’ll break down:
✅ What Gatherers are and why they were introduced
✅ How they make your streams more reusable, flexible, and powerful
✅ Built-in Gatherers like scan, windowFixed, windowSliding, mapConcurrent, and more
✅ Real-world examples comparing Stream vs Gatherers
✅ When to use Gatherers over normal Streams

👉 By the end of this video, you’ll understand why Gatherers are called “the next evolution of Streams” and how you can start using them to simplify your code.
